subject: physics
title: Energy Production Adventure 1: Energy sources and efficiency
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare energy sources — fossil, nuclear, renewable.
meta_desc: IBDP Physics — primary vs secondary energy, fossil fuels, renewables, efficiency, Sankey diagrams.
final_note: You learned primary (fossil, nuclear, solar) → secondary (electricity); efficiency = useful/total; Sankey diagrams visualise losses.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Non-renewable: coal, oil, gas (fossil), uranium (nuclear). Concentrated, on-demand, but emit CO₂ or radioactive waste.

Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass, tidal. Sustainable, low-emission, but variable.

Global mix (2022): ~80% fossil, ~5% nuclear, ~15% renewable — and slowly shifting.

η = E_useful / E_total × 100%

- Coal plant ~35%.
- Combined-cycle gas ~60%.
- Hydro ~90%.
- Solar PV ~20%.
- LED bulb ~90% (incandescent ~5%).

Second law: some energy ALWAYS lost as heat. No perfect engine.

Sankey shows energy flow with arrow widths ∝ amount.

Car: chemical (fuel) → useful KE (~25%) + waste heat (~50%) + friction (~15%) + air resistance (~10%).

Energy is conserved (1st law) but quality degrades (entropy ↑) — climate change forces honest accounting globally.
